about: What each collection step needs, least privilege first: the Entra or service role that grants the read, the delegated Graph scopes on the TenantKeep app, and the licence when the API answers only for licensed tenants. Errors name these so a failed run says what to grant. A role list is any-of. Entries marked verify are not yet confirmed by the least-privilege live run (plan Phase 3).

Entra.note: Global Reader reads every Entra setting the collector uses.

SignIns.licence: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2
SignIns.note: The sign-in log is kept 30 days; a free tenant has none to read.

Intune.note: Global Reader reads Intune configuration (verify); an Intune Read Only Operator role assignment also works.

Defender.note: Defender for Endpoint data also needs read access to the device groups in Defender unified RBAC when it is turned on (verify).

Exchange.note: Global Reader reads every Exchange setting the collector uses (seen on a least-privilege run, 2026-11-20). View-Only Organization Management is the Exchange-only alternative. Exchange Administrator works too but can change everything; this run only reads.

Purview.note: Global Reader reads sensitivity labels, DLP, retention, alert policies and role groups (seen on a least-privilege run, 2026-11-20). It does not read Insider Risk, Communication Compliance, audit retention policies or eDiscovery cases: those have role groups of their own, named per step, and their checks show as not evaluated without them. The TenantKeep Posture (view only) role group exists only where deploy/setup/New-PosturePurviewApp.ps1 created it, for the scheduled run's app.

SharePoint.note: The tenant settings read is refused to Global Reader (verify in Phase 3).

Teams.note: Global Reader reads the Teams tenant configuration (verify).

roles: Security Reader (on each subscription, for Defender for Cloud)
Azure.note: Azure roles, granted on the subscriptions or a management group, not in Entra.

PowerBI.note: The account also needs a Power BI or Fabric licence (the free one counts) and to have opened the Power BI portal once. The permission is optional and approved from the second consent link. A scheduled run needs no role: its identity is in a security group the Fabric tenant setting for read-only admin APIs names.

PowerPlatform.note: There is no read-only role and no read-only permission for these settings; the module's request entry point is what keeps the read a read. Optional, approved from the second consent link. Not collected in a scheduled run.

steps.note: App centric management: Get-M365UnifiedTenantSettings and Get-AllM365TeamsApps (AppName from MicrosoftTeams 7.3.0). A tenant not moved yet falls back to the app permission policy. Seen on a live run 2026-11-21: with the one sign-in the Teams module asks for a token to substrate.office.com that the session does not carry, so both steps report Not readable with this sign-in and CL-014 has no answer, unless the run was started with -TeamsAppSignIn: the Teams module then signs in by itself with a device code (verify on a live run).

The service status needs BackupRestore-Control.Read.All, which Microsoft documents for backup controller applications and the module does not ask for: it is read when Graph allows and unknown otherwise. Seen on a live run 2026-11-21: a Global Administrator with the permission consented was refused the policies as well, in a tenant without Microsoft 365 Backup; the step then reports Not readable with this sign-in (verify whether a tenant with the service on answers).
